title: Pride Closed His Ears Before It Destroyed His Life
paragraphs:
Pride Closed His Ears Before It Destroyed His Life
The Sin That Makes You Unteachable, Uncorrectable, and Slowly Pulls You Away from God Without You Even Realizing It
Some people don't fall away from God because they stopped believing.
They fall away because they stopped listening.
Not to sermons.
Not to parents.
Not to pastors.
Not to wise friends.
Most tragically... they stopped listening to God Himself.
Pride rarely announces itself with arrogance.
It usually disguises itself as certainty.
"I already know."
"They don't understand me."
"I've prayed about it."
"Nobody can tell me what to do."
"I'm different."

That is exactly why pride is one of the most dangerous sins in Scripture. It blinds without looking like blindness. It hardens while convincing the heart it is still soft. It makes correction sound offensive and wisdom seem unnecessary.
Long before destruction arrives, pride quietly seals the ears.
The Bible repeatedly warns us because God loves us too much to let us destroy ourselves without warning.
Proverbs says,
"Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall." (Proverbs 16:18, ESV)
The Hebrew word translated "pride" is גָּאוֹן (ga'on). It carries the idea of exaltation, swelling, lifting oneself higher than is proper. It describes a heart inflated beyond reality.
The phrase "before destruction" comes from the Hebrew לִפְנֵי־שֶׁבֶר (lifnei-shever).
Shever literally means breaking, collapse, ruin, or crushing.
God is not merely saying pride comes before embarrassment.
He is saying pride walks ahead of complete collapse.
The tragedy is that most people never recognize pride because they assume pride always looks loud.
Sometimes pride is simply refusing correction.
Sometimes pride is refusing accountability.
Sometimes pride is refusing to admit you were wrong.
Sometimes pride sounds incredibly spiritual.
"I don't need advice. God speaks directly to me."
But Scripture never teaches isolated Christianity.
God often speaks through His Word, His Spirit, and His people.
Proverbs 12:15 declares,
"The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, but a wise man listens to advice."
The Hebrew word for fool is אֱוִיל ('evil).
This is not someone with low intelligence.
It describes someone morally stubborn.
Someone who refuses correction.
Someone who believes his own judgment above wisdom.
Notice something astonishing.
The fool thinks he is right.
That is what makes pride terrifying.
Pride rarely feels like pride.
It feels like confidence.
The wise person, however, remains teachable.
The Hebrew word translated "listens" is שָׁמַע (shama').
This word means much more than hearing sounds.
It means to hear with the intention of obeying.
This same word is found in Deuteronomy 6:4.
"Hear, O Israel..."
The famous Shema.
God never merely wanted Israel to hear Him.
He wanted them to obey Him.
Biblical listening always changes behavior.
That is why wisdom is never measured by information.
Wisdom is measured by submission.
The New Testament carries the same warning.
James writes,
"God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble." (James 4:6)
The Greek word for "opposes" is ἀντιτάσσεται (antitassetai).
It literally describes arranging oneself in battle against another.
Think about that.
God is not merely disappointed with pride.
He actively resists it.
Not because He hates people.
Because pride destroys the people He loves.
Yet look at the second half.
"He gives grace."
The Greek word is χάρις (charis).
Undeserved favor.
Unearned kindness.
Divine generosity.
Grace always flows toward humility because humble hearts are open to receive what proud hearts reject.
Jesus demonstrated this beautifully.
The religious leaders believed they already knew everything.
Tax collectors listened.
Prostitutes repented.
Fishermen followed.
Children believed.
The proud debated.
The humble were transformed.
Perhaps that is why Jesus said,
"Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted." (Matthew 23:12)
The Greek word ὑψώσει (hypsosei) means to lift high.
God's kingdom works opposite the world's system.
The world says elevate yourself.
Jesus says surrender yourself.
The world says prove yourself.
Jesus says deny yourself.
The world says follow your heart.
Jesus says follow Me.
Pride believes surrender is weakness.
The Gospel reveals surrender is where true strength begins.
Peter understood this after years of failure.
The disciple who once declared he would never deny Jesus eventually wrote,
"Clothe yourselves, all of you, with humility toward one another..." (1 Peter 5:5)
The Greek word translated "clothe yourselves" is ἐγκομβώσασθε (egkombōsasthe).
It describes tying on the apron of a servant.
Many scholars believe Peter intentionally remembered Jesus washing the disciples' feet.
The King wore the clothing of a servant.
How could His followers wear anything else?
Perhaps the greatest irony about pride is this:
It often appears strongest moments before someone breaks.
The employee who ignores counsel.
The husband who refuses accountability.
The wife who rejects loving correction.
The teenager convinced everyone else is wrong.
The Christian who believes they have outgrown discipleship.
The leader who no longer accepts rebuke.
The believer who opens the Bible only to confirm what they already believe instead of allowing Scripture to correct them.
Every one of us is vulnerable.
That is why David prayed,
"Search me, O God, and know my heart! Try me and know my thoughts!" (Psalm 139:23)
David did not trust himself to detect his own pride.
Neither should we.
The Gospel gives us something pride never can.
Freedom to admit we are wrong.
Because our identity is no longer built on being right.
It is built on Christ who made us right with God.
Romans reminds us,
"But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us." (Romans 5:8)
Jesus did not wait for humble people.
He died for proud ones.
For stubborn ones.
For rebellious ones.
For people exactly like us.
The cross completely destroys pride because no one can stand before Calvary boasting.
We contributed nothing except the sin that made the cross necessary.
Everything else was grace.
Everything.
That is why our ministry exists under one simple conviction:
Every believer has a scandal.
Every redeemed believer has a Savior.
Jesus specializes in rewriting stories that seem beyond repair.
Maybe your pride has cost you friendships.
Maybe it damaged your marriage.
Maybe it has distanced you from your children.
Maybe it has kept you from apologizing.
Maybe it has convinced you that you already know enough about God.
Today, Christ invites you to lay it down.
Not because He wants to shame you.
Because He wants to heal you.
Humility is not thinking less of yourself.
It is thinking of Christ more than yourself.
The moment pride loosens its grip, grace rushes in.
Be honest before God.
You never know who God may reach through a simple act of obedience. Sometimes evangelism begins with one share.
Thank God for the people who love you enough to correct you with grace.
We all need reminders that God's wisdom is higher than our own.
If this ministry has blessed you, supporting it is one meaningful way to participate in spreading the Gospel and glorifying God through faithful biblical teaching.
The greatest tragedy is not being corrected.
The greatest tragedy is becoming too proud to hear the correction that could have saved you.
